description: How design-render resolves a theme's font stack and which metrics it lays text out with. A requested family resolves only to a face bundled here or to a generic family below; every other family is skipped and recorded as a substitution. The PPTX target names a typeface rather than a family keyword, so each generic family also documents the Office typeface a deck is written in. references/design-render.md explains the algorithm.

system-ui.note: The platform's interface face, with the platform's sans-serif as its own fallback.

monospace.note: The platform's default monospace face; every glyph advances the same width.

resolution_order: Walk the requested stack in order.
A family bundled in bundled_faces resolves to that face.
A generic family keyword resolves to its documented chain.
Any other family is skipped and recorded; the first resolvable member wins.
A stack with no resolvable member fails as font-unresolved, naming its first family.
The PPTX target writes a resolved generic family as its pptx_typeface, which Office ships, and records it in the deck's manifest beside the requested family; it embeds no font.
